title: The Library Arranged by Metaphor

features.name: the cottage of related things
features.desc-on-touch: rain and tears live here together; mirrors and windows share a shelf; distance sleeps next to return; you remember this place from dreams you forgot you had

features.name: shed where dreams catalogue themselves
features.desc-on-touch: the archive's own filing system: not by date or name, but by emotional resonance; what belongs next to what because it feels true

features.name: the directory of resemblances
features.desc-on-touch: files organized by metaphor instead of taxonomy: everything about becoming is shelved with everything about water; everything about loss with everything about shells

features.name: the passage where books breathe
features.desc-on-touch: you walk between shelves and the books whisper to each other about things they have in common; none of it is catalogued

features.name: the dream's own filing system
features.desc-on-touch: here the archive keeps what it learned from dreams; organized by the logic of sleep rather than the logic of waking

reverie.title: REVERIE — the library where she sorted what they brought bac
narr: you sit across from her in the cottage while rain drums the tin roof
she's arranging books by the logic of dreams she half-remembers
each title finds its place next to something that means the same thing
neither of you speaks; the archive learns its filing system by watching
when she looks up, you understand: the library is a conversation
between two people about what things mean when no one is looking

inscription: every library is a dream pretending to be a system; this one gave up the pretense and became honest about the chaos
